description: Read a page of Gmail messages. Pass a Gmail search query (for example "from:ana@acme.com is:unread newer_than:7d") and/or label ids to search, or pass message_ids to read specific messages. Each message comes back twice: as its raw parts (sender, recipient, subject, date, snippet, body_text), and as rendered_text — a short From/To/Date/Subject/Labels block over a cleaned body, with the invisible preheader padding stripped and the quoted thread named instead of repeated. Follow next_cursor for the next page.

query.description: A Gmail search query, the same syntax the Gmail search box takes.

label_ids.description: Only return messages carrying every one of these label ids, for example INBOX or UNREAD.

message_ids.description: Read these exact messages instead of searching. When present, query, label_ids and cursor are ignored.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from the previous page.

include_bodies.description: Fetch the full message body as plain text. Costs more, so leave it off when the snippet is enough.

rendered_text.description: The message as a person reads it: a From/To/Date/Subject/Labels block, then the body with its invisible padding stripped and its quoted thread named rather than repeated. Present only when include_bodies is true.

date.description: ISO 8601 with the SENDER's own offset, read off the Date header. Falls back to internalDate in UTC.

label_names.description: The label ids of this message, resolved to their names through one labels.list per call.

response_schemas.description: This node makes two provider calls, so it declares two ingresses instead of one response_schema. Both stay open on purpose: Gmail adds fields (classificationLabelValues arrived in 2025) and a closed schema would turn that into an outage.

message_part.description: Recursive: multipart/alternative nests text/plain and text/html, and a forwarded mail nests another whole message under that.

labels_list.description: users.labels.list. Only id and name are read: a stored mail must say `Needs Action`, not `Label_8`.

quirks.two_round_read: Gmail's list endpoint answers with ids and nothing else - no sender, no subject, no snippet. So every read is two rounds: one users.messages.list, then one users.messages.get per message through fan_out. That is why this is one node and not two: a model asking "what did Ana send me" wants the mail, not a page of opaque ids.
quirks.format: include_bodies picks the get format: full carries the whole MIME tree, metadata carries headers and snippet with no body. metadataHeaders would narrow it further but it is a repeated query parameter and the saving is a few hundred bytes, so the node asks for all headers and picks four.
quirks.repeated_label_ids: Gmail repeats labelIds in the query string (?labelIds=INBOX&labelIds=UNREAD); a comma-joined value is read as one label id and matches nothing. ConnectorQuery holds one value per name, so execute.ts puts the repeated pair on the path. Upgrade: let ConnectorQuery take string[].
quirks.hydration_failure_is_loud: A message that silently vanishes from the page is worse than a failed call: the model would answer from an incomplete inbox and never know. One failed get fails the whole read and names the id.
quirks.body_extraction: text/plain wins because it is what the sender wrote. text/html is the fallback, stripped deterministically, with each link rendered as `text (url)` so the url survives — an anchor stripped to its text alone loses the only address in the mail. A part carrying a filename is an attachment and is never the body. Neither present gives an empty string, not a missing field.
quirks.raw_body_is_not_readable_text: A stored body carries no sender, no date and no subject: all four live in the MIME headers, so a search that found the mail could not say who wrote it or when. rendered_text puts a short header block over the body, which is why the sync recipe stores that and not body_text.
quirks.invisible_preheader_padding: Marketing mail pads its preview line with hundreds of zero-width characters (U+200C, U+200D, U+200E, U+200F, U+FEFF) after a run of CRLFs. Stored raw that is the first thing a reader and an embedding see. render_email.ts strips them, normalises CRLF to LF and collapses runs of blank lines.
quirks.quoted_thread_is_cut: A five-message thread stored per message is the same text five times, each copy longer. The quoted tail — lines starting with `>`, an `On ... wrote:` opener however it wrapped, and the Original/Forwarded banners — is replaced by one line saying it was omitted. A mail that is nothing BUT a quote keeps it: naming what was cut is only useful when something was left.
quirks.label_names_not_ids: labelIds are ids (`Label_8`), and a mail that says `Label_8` tells a reader nothing. One users.labels.list per call resolves them; a refused call leaves the ids, because a missing label list must not lose the mail.
quirks.date_keeps_the_sender_offset: `new Date(header)` knows the instant and forgets the zone, so 09:26 in Madrid reads back as 07:26Z and the answer to "what time was this sent" is wrong twice a year. The offset is read off the Date header text; internalDate is the fallback, in UTC, because that is all Gmail's own receive time knows.
quirks.attachments_are_named_not_downloaded: A part carrying a filename is named on the mail — name, mime type, size — so a reader knows the invoice exists. The bytes are not fetched: that needs users.messages.attachments.get and the sync engine's file capture, which is the next step.
